pr_body:
Related issues:

Fixed #20115.

**Description**

This PR integrates `PMREMGenerator` such that cube maps and equirectangular environment maps are automatically converted to the cubeUV format for PBR materials.

Besides, `WebGLRenderer.setBackgroundBlurriness()` is added which allows to control the blurriness of skyboxes. This method also works when a cube or  equirectangular texture is assigned to `Scene.background` by converting these texture into the cubeUV format. It essentially addresses my feedback from https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/18241#issuecomment-569432416.

`webgl_loader_gltf` was the only example which was updated in this PR. The usage of `WebGLRenderer.setBackgroundBlurriness()` is important in this example otherwise the background would look very blocky (because of the nearest filtered HDR texture). I have applied a very blurred background for now (which you sometimes see in other engines):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12612165/95192741-e9aeb680-07d2-11eb-8e8c-6f5503f68976.png)
pr_comments: @mrdoob If you have concerns about `WebGLRenderer.setBackgroundBlurriness()`, it should be no problem to replace it later with your suggested API in #17420. This PR is mainly focused on integrating `PMREMGenerator` into the renderer. However, a control mechanism for a skybox's blurriness is required. Hence the addition of `WebGLRenderer.setBackgroundBlurriness()`.

I have encountered an issue during testing today. There is a problem when using a cube render target as an environment map for a PBR material. In this case, `WebGLCubeMaps` tries to convert it to cubeUV format which fails currently because `image.length === 6` is not true for cube render targets. `WebGLCubeMaps` return `null` right now and no environment map gets applied.

Besides, `WebGLCubeMaps` performs its conversions just once and not every time the render target is updated e.g. when using `CubeCamera`. On the other hand, it's not _really_ recommended to apply dynamic cube maps generated by `CubeCamera` to a PBR material since they are not pre-processed with `PMREMGenerator`. And performing the pre-processing with `PMREMGenerator` per frame is surely not good for performance anyway.

Um, it seems the only reliable way to make this more robust is to introduce some sort of flag or subclass that allows us to distinct textures of render targets from ordinary textures. In this way, `WebGLCubeMaps` could easily detect textures of render targets and exclude any automatic pre-processing of environment maps.
Can we leave the background blurriness for another PR? I think this PR should focus on integrating PMREM.

The current implementation uses the material to determine whether `PMREMGenerator` should be used or not. Meaning when using a PBR material with an equirectangular or cube map,  `WebGLCubeMaps` performs the conversion to the cubeUV format.

However, this workflow does not work for `WebGLBackground` since the skybox is rendered with a special shader material. And skyboxes should work no matter if you have meshes with PBR materials in your scene. 

So if there is no way to control the blurriness, the renderer does not know whether to blur the skybox or not. This is required though otherwise it is not possible to replicate the current looks of the examples. Meaning if the feature is missing, the background will lock blocky because of the nearest filtered HDR textures.

The only workaround would be to ask the user to use `PMREMGenerator` on application level in order to produce a cubeUV texture for `Scene.background`. However, this would be a bit contradictory to the actual goal of the PR: The avoidance of `PMREMGenerator` on application level.

The issue becomes more clear if you download the branch and remove the line `renderer.setBackgroundBlurriness( 0.5 );` from `webgl_loader_gltf`. The skybox will look blocky. I'm not sure how a different implementation should look like so `WebGLBackground` always requests the correct env map from `WebGLCubeMaps`.

Hmm, okay.
I need to give it a go myself so I have a good understanding of the problem.
Will use this PR as reference.
Hmm, could you try splitting `WebGLCubeMaps` into `WebGLCubeMaps` and `WebGLCubeUVMaps`?

I've tried this before but it means we need at each place where `cubemaps.get()` is now called additional (and thus redundant) code. Because it's necessary to distinct whether `WebGLCubeMaps` or `WebGLCubeUVMaps` should be used. 

If we want to go this route, we probably need an additional component that handles this. Maybe `WebGLEnvMaps`?

> I've tried this before but it means we need at each place where `cubemaps.get()` is now called additional (and thus redundant) code. Because it's necessary to distinct whether `WebGLCubeMaps` or `WebGLCubeUVMaps` should be used. 

Wouldn't moving the logic outside be something like this?

```js
materialProperties.envMap = ( material.isMeshStandardMaterial ? cubeuvmaps : cubemap ).get( material.envMap || environment );
```
Um...I'm not sure anymore to be honest 😅 .
Sorry, I have to dive into this topic again. There are different ways how `cubemaps.get()` or `cubeuvmaps.get()` could be called and I have to verify all of them.

> Hmm, could you try splitting WebGLCubeMaps into WebGLCubeMaps and WebGLCubeUVMaps?

Okay, this worked fine! But it's still necessary to solve the render target issue (especially the case when a cube render target is dynamically updated with `CubeCamera` and used as an environment map).

I've introduced `isRenderTargetTexture` to detect textures which are owned by render targets. In this way, it's possible to not break existing code and make auto-conversion more robust. It makes `CubeTexture._needsFlipEnvMap` obsolete, too.

The policy is that the engine does not auto-convert environment maps if they are textures of render targets. In this case, the user has to do it if desired.

/bump

I support both the integration of PMREM and background blurriness.

However, I really would like to have the `MeshStandardMaterial` and `MeshPhysicalMaterial` shaders only support `CUBE_UV` environment maps, because only `CUBE_UV` maps work correctly.

So... supporting the auto-conversion of any user-specified `Standard/Physical` environment map to PMREM would be ideal.

We could then remove PMREM from the API -- or keep it as a /jsm utility if users want to create their own PMREMs.

@Mugen87 Is that doable at this point, or are there still "gotchas" to deal with?

> However, I really would like to have the MeshStandardMaterial and MeshPhysicalMaterial shaders only support CUBE_UV environment maps, because only CUBE_UV maps work correctly.

Makes sense. But since it's a breaking change and for simplicity reasons, I would make a different PR for this.

> We could then remove PMREM from the API -- or keep it as a /jsm utility if users want to create there own PMREMs.

I suggest to keep it in order to not break existing code. At some point in the future it's maybe okay to make the class internal.

> Is that doable at this point, or are there still "gotchas" to deal with?

I think the PR was considered to be "complete". However, if we agree on an API I would make a fresh one since the existing merge conflicts are already severe.

>But since it's a breaking change

What would break?

Sorry, I've mixed topics. After studying the code again cube uv is in fact the only supported format of PBR materials since the other two (equirect and cubemap) are converted. So it's just a matter of cleaning up the obsolete code.

>So it's just a matter of cleaning up the obsolete code.

... in the shader. And I'll do that as a second step if you can automate the computation of PMREM. 😇

> And to clarify, equirect is converted to cube map currently, but for PBR materials, it will have to be converted directly to PMREM, instead.

Correct! That is the goal of this PR!
Closing in favor of #22178.

issue_context.title: WebGLRenderer: Integrate PMREM
issue_context.body:
With the introduction of `WebGLCubeMaps`, the engine has now a mechanism to internally convert environment maps. I've quickly hacked in `PMREMGenerator` support today and it is actually possible to perform the conversion used in [webgl_loader_gltf](https://threejs.org/examples/webgl_loader_gltf). It would love to see PMREM integrated in the renderer since it's a technical detail most users should not care about.

However, my implementation is a hack right now since it's not defined _when_ `PMREMGenerator` should do its work. The question is: How can `WebGLCubeMaps` detect textures that should be processed by `PMREMGenerator`?
comments: I think @WestLangley was exploring this too.

I hacked in the same thing a few days ago as a proof-of-concept, and it worked beautifully - but not reliably, because I was not focused on that part.

Automatic PMREM conversion should only apply to equirectangular and cube environment maps for `MeshStandardMaterial` and `MeshPhysicalMaterial`. I created `WebGLCubeUVMaps` to do that.

IMO, `CubeUVMaps` should not be used for blurry `scene.background` because they are currently too blocky for that purpose. JMO.
@WestLangley Okay, I leave this topic up to you 👍 . And yeah depending on the code complexity a separate `WebGLCubeUVMaps` makes sense.
@Mugen87 This implementation details are a bit tedious (as we have discovered), so I likely will not be the one to file the PR. But I will help at the appropriate time in any other way I can. :-)
@WestLangley Okay^^. Have you already pushed your changes into a branch of your fork?

Yes, I have found that PMREM is not good for background blurriness. It is too blocky.

Personally, I would like to see `Phong` removed -- or moved to the examples somehow -- and perhaps replaced with `MeshSpecGlossMaterial`; the latter is full-featured; `Phong` is not.

I suppose `Lambert` will have to be retained as it supports Gouraud shading.

I don't think we have to remove materials in context of this issue.

The goal should be adding support for background blurriness (with cube maps) and automatic PMREM conversion for PBR materials.

In general I do not vote to remove build-in materials from the core since this would break a lot of user code. Instead I vote to reconsider the material support for `WebGPURenderer`.

@WestLangley said:

>Personally, I would like to see Phong removed -- or moved to the examples somehow

I was reiterating _exactly_ what @mrdoob said to me offline. I happen to agree.

I prefer to see the library improved, and not held back by outdated illumination models. We have moved code to the examples before, and can do so again. Users will be just fine.

I suggest we open a new issue for what materials should be supported in the future. TBH, it's off-topic regarding this issue.

> Users will be just fine.

Again, it seems you view on this topic (backwards compatibility) does not reflect how users _actually_ react on changes to the library. The project has to be way more carefully than before when things are removed. Only because it was done in the past, it does not mean it was the right way to do so.

> Against this backdrop, I wonder if it makes more sense to solve #18241 first and then focus on PMREM integration.

I've changed my mind here. I think it's better if `Scene.background` also uses cubeUV until the project comes up with a solution for #18241. In this way, there will be no visual difference when the automatic conversion is used.
@mrdoob suggested moving Phong to the examples, and I was working on that in my fork, but given @Mugen87 is going to block it, it no longer makes sense for me to pursue it at this point.

review_comments:
```js
( isCubeMap && image && image.length === 6 )
```
This line was actually buggy. `image.length === 6` is not safe for testing if cube textures are complete. The cube texture loader doesn't load the single images in order so the array can have a length of six although images are still missing.
